title: Passkey (WebAuthn/FIDO2) Authentication in Identity
description: Implement passwordless authentication using passkeys (WebAuthn/FIDO2) in ASP.NET Core Identity with .NET 10.

data.text: Passkeys are a phishing-resistant, passwordless authentication method based on the WebAuthn standard and FIDO2 protocol. Instead of typing a password, users authenticate using a biometric (fingerprint, Face ID) or a platform authenticator (Windows Hello, Touch ID). The private key never leaves the device, making passkeys significantly more secure than traditional passwords.

.NET 10 adds built-in support for passkey registration and sign-in through ASP.NET Core Identity. The new PasskeyManager service and WebAuthn integration handle the cryptographic ceremony, credential storage, and challenge validation for you.

data.content: Register passkey services and add the passkey sign-in page

data.text: The passkey registration flow follows the standard WebAuthn ceremony: the server generates a challenge, the browser requests a new credential from the authenticator, the user authenticates with their biometric or PIN, and the credential public key is sent back to the server and stored in the Identity system.

data.title: Passkey vs Password
data.text: Passkeys replace passwords entirely for users who opt in. You can offer both options during a transition period. Each user can have multiple passkeys registered for different devices.

Passkeys are stored in the Identity system alongside existing credentials. Each passkey record includes the credential ID, public key, signature counter, and user-supplied name (e.g., 'MacBook Pro Touch ID'). Users can manage their passkeys from their account page — adding new ones for additional devices and removing ones they no longer use.

data.title: Benefits of Passkey Authentication
items: Phishing-resistant — credentials are bound to the originating domain.
No password to steal, phish, or leak in a data breach.
Biometric authentication is fast and familiar to users.
Cross-device sync via iCloud Keychain or Google Password Manager.

data.title: Summary
points: Use AddPasskeySupport() to enable passkeys in ASP.NET Core Identity.
The WebAuthn ceremony is handled by built-in services — no external packages needed.
Users can register multiple passkeys for different devices.
Passkeys can coexist with password-based authentication during a transition period.
data.takeaway: Passkey support in .NET 10 Identity makes passwordless authentication accessible with minimal setup, offering a more secure and user-friendly alternative to passwords.
